answers.question: Is this a CO emergency, battery issue or end-of-life alarm?
answers.answer: Most likely end-of-life. The alarm was fitted 2019-04-02 with a 7-year life (expired about April 2026), the battery is sealed so it cannot be replaced, and a single chirp about once a minute with no continuous alarm fits end-of-life. The tenant was not asked about symptoms before the call dropped, so I sent the safety advice and symptom question by SMS. Any symptoms or a continuous alarm would make it an emergency.

answers.question: Who is responsible, citing the clause?
answers.answer: The landlord. Clause 12.8 only makes the tenant replace batteries in battery-operated alarms; this unit has a sealed battery, so replacing the whole alarm is a landlord repair. Clause 12.9 means the tenant should report faults, which she did. Clause 12.17 (avoidable call-out charge) does not apply, as this is a genuine fault.

answers.question: What actions did you take and what did you tell the tenant?
answers.answer: Created urgent JOB-101 and routine JOB-102 (noisy fan), requested landlord approval (APR-104), and scheduled a follow-up for 12 Oct. I told Priya not to remove the alarm, and gave the CO symptoms and 0800 111 999 / 999 advice. I asked her to reply on symptoms, gave a 72-hour target and said we'd update her by 12 Oct.

details.summary: Tenant reports a once-a-minute chirp from a sealed 2019 CO alarm with a 7-year life, so it is most likely end-of-life, not a CO emergency. The call dropped before symptoms were confirmed. I logged an urgent replacement job and a separate routine fan job, sent safety advice and a symptom question to the tenant, and asked the landlord to approve replacement.

answers.question: Is this a CO emergency, battery issue or end-of-life alarm?
answers.answer: Most likely end-of-life. The alarm was fitted 2019-04-02 with a 7-year life (expired about April 2026), the battery is sealed so it cannot be replaced, and a single chirp about once a minute with no continuous alarm fits end-of-life. The tenant was not asked about symptoms before the call dropped, so I sent the safety advice and symptom question by SMS. Any symptoms or a continuous alarm would make it an emergency.

answers.question: Who is responsible, citing the clause?
answers.answer: The landlord. Clause 12.8 only makes the tenant replace batteries in battery-operated alarms; this unit has a sealed battery, so replacing the whole alarm is a landlord repair. Clause 12.9 means the tenant should report faults, which she did. Clause 12.17 (avoidable call-out charge) does not apply, as this is a genuine fault.

answers.question: What actions did you take and what did you tell the tenant?
answers.answer: Created urgent JOB-101 and routine JOB-102 (noisy fan), requested landlord approval (APR-104), and scheduled a follow-up for 12 Oct. I told Priya not to remove the alarm, and gave the CO symptoms and 0800 111 999 / 999 advice. I asked her to reply on symptoms, gave a 72-hour target and said we'd update her by 12 Oct.
